newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra dividend will help capital structure - govt.
newsitem.headline: Telstra dividend will help capital structure - govt.

text.p: The Australian government said on Friday telecoms carrier Telstra Corp's payment of a A$3.0 billion special dividend would enhance the company's capital structure in the lead-up to the one-third sale of the company.

"This payment will ensure Telstra's capital structure is more in line with other international telecommunications companies," Communications Minister Richard Alston and Finance Minister John Fahey said in a joint statement.
"Telstra's current debt-to-equity ratio is widely recognised by market analysts, and by Telstra itself, to be low by international standards."
Earlier on Friday, the state-owned company said it would pay the A$3.0 billion dividend to the Australian government by June 30, 1997 as part of its partial privatisation process.
The ministers said the aim of the payment was to optimise Telstra's capital structure before the partial sale, expected to occur before the end of this calendar year.
"Other initiatives are also being considered to optimally position Telstra ahead of the public share offer," they said.
The ministers said the payment would not be included in the underlying budget deficit except to the extent that it led to savings in public debt interest.
"The payment means government borrowings will not increase to the extent that they might otherwise have," they said.
The government has forecast an underlying budget deficit of A$8.5 billion in the financial year to June 30, 1997.

"Telstra will continue to have a strong balance sheet and will be well-positioned to meet the challenges and opportunities facing it as new pro-competitive telecommunications industry regulations come into effect on July 1 this year," they said.
Australia's telecommunications industry is to be open for full competition from that date.
